claims.statement: The pinned completion-switch fragment says available models change and a one-model inventory yields a single picker option. Switching inline suggestions does not change chat or next-edit models; it also states no change to data collection/use policy, which is not proof identical processing or data destination behavior.

The fragment says Free completions consume the quota regardless of chosen model and public-code-match settings apply regardless of model choice. The prerelease-filter caveat reviewed in DOCS-COPILOTFILTERINSTRUCTIONS-003 prevents interpreting this configuration statement as guaranteed effective filtering for every model.

The completion switcher is described as enabled automatically for Free and Pro, while its inspected editor-preview include requires provider organization/enterprise enablement for Business or Enterprise. Product availability and policy conditions must be retained alongside editor prerequisites; no target configuration verified.

The JetBrains switching prerequisites require an alternative model currently available and latest IDE plus latest Copilot extension. Their conjunction and moving version requirement do not certify installed readiness.
The Visual Studio switching prerequisites require an available alternative and version 17.14 Preview 2 or newer; this threshold is different from the latest-version wording for other IDEs.
The VS Code switching prerequisites require an available alternative plus latest editor and Copilot extension. A visible picker or subscription alone does not prove all requirements.

The chat code-reference fragment says responses containing public-repository matching code indicate a link at the response end to view details in the editor. This mechanism is not exhaustive provenance detection, accuracy assurance or license permission.

The inline-reference fragment says accepting matching suggestions records source file URLs and a license name if found, enabling a subsequent decision about attribution or removal. Discovered license metadata alone is not per-file legal clearance, and absence of a license entry is not permission.

The inline-reference note excludes manually written code and altered suggestions from its accepted-suggestion match checks. It reports matches typically below one percent of suggestions, a historical descriptive claim rather than a measured rate here; no references cannot be treated as no infringement or complete match coverage.
